summary: Same skeleton — an N-colour, L-pixel repeating sequence that chases along the strip with crossfade, twinkle and blink dials — and ColorLength / NumberOfColorsUsed / ColorSmoothing / colour order match exactly, but the port chases in the OPPOSITE direction at ~1/17 the speed, mirrors and grossly weakens the FadeOut envelope, barely responds to TwinkleWhite / TwinkleOff / Blink, ships different default colours and defaults, and exposes its colour controls as hsvPicker instead of rgbPicker.
observations: Both sides are alive, compile clean, error-free, single-regime and steady: a 240 s / 2 fps survey and a --skip 120 late window show the same chase at t=0 and t=130 on both (orig mean 42 / port mean 85 throughout, brightnessTrend steady, no decay or freeze).

CONTROL SURFACE MISMATCH: original exposes 12 rgbPicker controls named rgbPickerColor_1..rgbPickerColor_12 (labels Color_1..Color_12); port exposes 12 hsvPicker controls named hsvPickerColor1..hsvPickerColor12 (labels Color1..Color12). Different kind, different names/labels. The 8 sliders (ColorLength, ChaseSpeed, FadeOut, ColorSmoothing, TwinkleWhite, TwinkleOff, Blink, NumberOfColorsUsed) match by name and kind on both; only the listing order differs (orig sliders-then-pickers, port pickers-then-sliders).

UNTOUCHED DEFAULTS DIVERGE. Original (dump at t=0): 4-pixel repeat, per group [250,0,0] [4,0,250] [0,0,4] [0,0,0] — 1-px red, 1-px blue, a dim decay pixel and a black gap; mean brightness 42; drifts RIGHT at +0.39 px/s with smooth sub-pixel crossfade (red peak walks pixel 0 -> pixel 1 between t=0 and t=3, values 250->0 while its neighbour goes 4->207). Port: 10-pixel repeat, 5 px of pure [255,0,0] then 5 px of pure [0,0,255], no dark gap and no fade; mean brightness 85 (exactly 2x the original); drifts LEFT at -0.20 px/s in hard whole-pixel jumps (119 of 120 baseline frames post motion 0, then one 1-px step).

DEFAULT PALETTE DIFFERS. With NumberOfColorsUsed=1 and ColorLength=0 (12 colours x 1 px) the original renders red, blue, then TEN BLACK pixels — colour slots 3..12 default to off. The port renders red,blue,red,blue,... — its slots 3..12 default to alternating red/blue. Probe agrees: orig Color_1..Color_4 responsive and Color_5..Color_12 inert (default NumberOfColorsUsed = 4 colours), port Color1..Color2 responsive and Color3..Color12 inert (default = 2 colours).

CHASE DIRECTION IS INVERTED. Measured by chaining circular cross-correlation of --dump'ed frames (2 colours x 5 px, period 10, dumps 0.025 s apart): at ChaseSpeed=1 the original moves +78.6 px/s (rightward) and the port -4.7 px/s (leftward); at ChaseSpeed=0 the signs flip on both. Confirmed without correlation by raw pixel trace at ChaseSpeed=0.8: the original's red block sits at index 1 (t=0), 3 (t=1), 5 (t=2) — rightward — while the port is frozen. The same inversion holds at default settings (orig +0.39 px/s, port -0.20 px/s).

CHASE SPEED IS ~17-26x TOO SLOW ON THE PORT. Full slider curve (px/s, orig vs port): 0.0 -78.6/+4.7, 0.1 -18.3/+0.7, 0.2 -2.0/0.0, 0.3-0.7 0.0/0.0, 0.8 +2.0/0.0, 0.9 +18.3/-0.7, 1.0 +78.6/-4.7. Both are symmetric about 0.5 and both have a wide dead zone, but the port's dead zone is wider (dead at 0.2 and 0.8 where the original still moves 2 px/s) and its top speed is 4.7 px/s against the original's 78.6 px/s.

Both sides are frame-rate INDEPENDENT: the same chained-shift measurement gives orig 78.5 px/s and port -4.6 px/s at both --fps 20 and --fps 40, and orig 80 px/s at --fps 100 and --fps 200. No frame-rate coupling on either side.

FADEOUT IS MIRRORED AND FAR WEAKER. 2 colours x 12 px, chase stopped, smoothing 0. Original at FadeOut=0.25 ramps each block 19,25,32,41,53,68,86,108,135,167,207,255 — dim at the block's low-index end, full at its high-index end (~0.79x per pixel decay away from the bright edge). Port at 0.25 goes 255,251,247,...,213 — bright at the LOW-index end, only 1.2x total falloff (~0.983x/px). At FadeOut=1 the original leaves a single lit pixel per block (0,0,...,4,255) while the port ramps 255,196,147,...,1,0 across the whole block. Relative to each side's own (opposite) chase direction both tails trail the motion, so the port reads as a mirror image of the original, but its fade slider is roughly an order of magnitude gentler at every setting.

COLOUR ORDER IS CORRECT. With Color1/2/3 explicitly set to red/green/blue on both sides (rgbPicker 1,0,0 / 0,1,0 / 0,0,1 vs hsvPicker 0,1,1 / 0.3333,1,1 / 0.6667,1,1), both render 255,0,0 | 0,255,0 | 0,0,255 repeating left-to-right — identical, and the pickers agree on the colours they produce.

TWINKLEWHITE: the original DIMS the whole strip to ~25% as soon as the dial leaves 0 (mean 85 -> 21.3 at 0.1) and its spark density rises with the dial (meanG 0.2 at 0.1 -> 4.2 at 1.0); sparks fade in and out over several frames (visible as vertical smears in the waterfall). The port keeps the base at full brightness (mean ~80 at every setting) and lays 1-frame white dots on top at a density that does not change with the dial (meanG pinned at ~10-11 from 0.1 to 1.0).

TWINKLEOFF: the original blanks progressively more pixels as the dial rises (mean 78.9 at 0.1 -> 54.3 at 1.0, motion 0 -> 13.9, dropouts re-rolled essentially every frame). The port's blanking is nearly dial-independent (mean 67.5 -> 70.6 across 0.1..1.0, motion 0 -> 1.7) and its dark pixels persist for many frames, reading as thick vertical bars rather than fine noise.

BLINK: the original's dial is a frequency knob — over a 20 s window it produces 2 blinks at 0.1/0.25/0.4, 5 at 0.6, 11 at 0.75, 23 at 0.9, each blink a single 50 ms all-off frame, delivered at Blink=1 as bursts of three 1-frame strobes every ~2 s. The port produces 2-3 blinks in 20 s at EVERY setting with no trend, and each blink is a ~0.5 s blackout (10-13 frames).

At matched non-trivial dials (4 colours R/G/B/Y, ColorLength 0.3, ChaseSpeed 0.9, FadeOut 0.5, ColorSmoothing 0.3) the two look plainly different: original = sparse bright dots on mostly black racing rightward (mean 23, motion 44); port = wide full-brightness colour bands with a soft gradient creeping leftward (mean 72, motion 5).
Randomness is not the issue: seeds 1, 7 and 1234 give the same statistical character on each side and the same orig/port gap (orig mean 23 vs port mean 68 at TwinkleWhite=1, TwinkleOff=0.5).

dials.name: NumberOfColorsUsed
dials.origEffect: sets sequence length in colour slots; 0->1, 0.2->3, 0.4->5, 0.6->7, 0.8->9, 1->12 slots, unused slots default to black
dials.portEffect: identical slot-count mapping (0->1, 0.2->3, ... 1->12), but slots 3+ default to alternating red/blue instead of black

dials.name: ColorLength
dials.portEffect: byte-identical mapping at every value tested

dials.name: ChaseSpeed
dials.origEffect: 0.5 = stopped, symmetric; 0.8->+2 px/s, 0.9->+18.3, 1.0->+78.6 px/s rightward, mirrored below 0.5
dials.portEffect: same symmetry and dead zone but INVERTED direction and ~17x slower: 0.8->0, 0.9->-0.7, 1.0->-4.7 px/s leftward

dials.name: FadeOut
dials.origEffect: aggressive per-block brightness ramp, bright at the block's trailing-motion edge; 0.25 already a 13x ramp, 1.0 leaves a single lit pixel
dials.portEffect: mirrored ramp direction and ~10x gentler; 0.25 gives only a 1.2x falloff, 1.0 a smooth full-block decay

dials.name: ColorSmoothing
dials.origEffect: crossfade width between adjacent colours; identical to port at 0 (hard edge) and 1 (full linear blend)
dials.portEffect: same shape and endpoints, but the mid-range curve is more linear — port at 0.25 blends about as much as orig at 0.5

dials.name: TwinkleWhite
dials.origEffect: dims the whole strip to ~25% and adds multi-frame white sparks whose density scales with the dial (meanG 0.2->4.2)
dials.portEffect: no global dim (base stays full) and 1-frame white dots at a fixed density that ignores the dial (meanG ~10-11 throughout)

dials.name: TwinkleOff
dials.origEffect: fine per-frame random blanking whose density rises with the dial (mean 78.9->54.3, motion 0->13.9)
dials.portEffect: coarse multi-frame blanking at a nearly dial-independent density (mean ~68-71, motion 0->1.7)

dials.name: Blink
dials.origEffect: blink frequency knob: 2 blinks/20 s at 0.1 up to 23 at 0.9, each a single 50 ms all-off frame (triple-strobe bursts every ~2 s at 1.0)
dials.portEffect: 2-3 blinks/20 s at every setting with no trend, each a ~0.5 s blackout

dials.name: Color_1..Color_12 (port: Color1..Color12)
dials.origEffect: rgbPicker per slot; slot colours appear left-to-right in slot order; slots beyond NumberOfColorsUsed unused; defaults red, blue, then black
dials.portEffect: hsvPicker per slot — different control KIND and different names (no underscore); same left-to-right slot order and same rendered colours when set explicitly, but defaults are red/blue repeating for all 12 slots

feedback: Flip the chase direction. At ChaseSpeed>0.5 the original translates the sequence toward HIGHER pixel indices (right); the port translates toward lower indices. At ChaseSpeed=1 the original is +78.6 px/s and the port is -4.7 px/s (measured on 2 colours x 5 px, period 10).

Scale the chase speed up by ~17x and widen the live range. Target curve, px/s at ChaseSpeed = 0/0.1/0.2/0.3-0.7/0.8/0.9/1.0: -78.6 / -18.3 / -2.0 / 0 / +2.0 / +18.3 / +78.6. The port currently reads 0 at 0.2 and 0.8, where the original already moves 2 px/s, and tops out at 4.7 px/s.

Mirror the FadeOut envelope and make it far steeper. On a 12-px block with chase stopped and smoothing 0, the original at FadeOut=0.25 should read 19,25,32,41,53,68,86,108,135,167,207,255 (dim at the low-index end, ~0.79x per pixel); the port currently reads 255,251,...,213 — both reversed and ~10x too gentle. At FadeOut=1 the original leaves essentially one lit pixel per block (0,...,4,255) while the port decays gently across the whole block.

Default colour slots 3..12 to OFF, not to alternating red/blue. Set NumberOfColorsUsed to 12 with 1 px per colour and the original draws red, blue, then ten black pixels; the port draws red/blue repeating.

Fix the untouched defaults: the original starts at 4 colours x 1 px (period 4) with a visible fade tail and a black gap, mean brightness 42, drifting right at +0.39 px/s with SUB-PIXEL interpolation. The port starts at 2 colours x 5 px (period 10), no fade, mean 85, and creeps left at 0.20 px/s in hard whole-pixel jumps — 119 of 120 baseline frames register zero motion. Sub-pixel crossfade of the chase position is missing, not just a speed difference.

TwinkleWhite must dim the base. In the original any non-zero TwinkleWhite drops overall brightness from 85 to ~21 and the white sparks fade in/out over several frames; the port keeps the base at ~80 and flashes single-frame dots. Also make spark density track the dial: the original's meanG goes 0.2 (dial 0.1) -> 4.2 (dial 1.0) while the port's sits at ~10-11 regardless.

Make TwinkleOff density track its dial and re-roll every frame: the original goes mean 78.9 -> 54.3 and motion 0 -> 13.9 across dial 0.1 -> 1.0; the port stays at mean ~70 / motion <2 and its dropouts persist for many frames as thick dark bars.

Rebuild Blink as a frequency control with 1-frame strobes. Over a 20 s window the original gives 2, 2, 2, 5, 11, 23 blinks at dial 0.1/0.25/0.4/0.6/0.75/0.9, each a single 50 ms all-off frame (and at 1.0 arrives as bursts of three strobes every ~2 s). The port gives 2-3 blinks at every dial value, each a ~0.5 s blackout.

Change the colour controls from hsvPicker to rgbPicker and name them Color_1..Color_12 (with the underscore) to match the original's surface; also list the eight sliders before the pickers as the original does. The rendered colours already agree once set, so only the control kind, names and ordering need changing.
